hints: Notice the starting positions: $20 \text{ N}$ on the left and $15 \text{ N}$ on the right. A clockwise pulley rotation lifts the left string and lowers the right string.
Connect rotation to vertical distance with arc length $s = r\theta$, where $r = 0.40 \text{ m}$ and $\theta = 60^{\circ}$ must be in radians $\pi/3$.
Combine the two gravitational potential changes as gain minus loss: $\Delta E_p = 20s - 15s = 5s$, then evaluate $s$ numerically.
walkthrough: Clockwise rotation makes the left side move up and the right side move down, so the $20 \text{ N}$ weight rises a distance $s$ and the $15 \text{ N}$ weight falls the same distance $s$.
The string moves by the arc length on the pulley of radius $r = 0.40 \text{ m}$. Convert $\theta = 60^{\circ}$ to radians: $\theta = 60/360 \times 2\pi = \pi/3 \approx 1.05 \text{ rad}$.
Use $\Delta E_p = W\Delta h$. Gain for $20 \text{ N}$ is $20 \times 0.419 \approx 8.38 \text{ J}$ and loss for $15 \text{ N}$ is $15 \times 0.419 \approx 6.28 \text{ J}$.
Net increase is gain minus loss: $\Delta E_{total} = (20-15) \times 0.419 = 5 \times 0.419 \approx 2.09 \text{ J}$, about $2.1 \text{ J}$ with unit $\text{J}$. This is option C.
